findings.description: The source code contains repeated comments instructing the reviewer not to install or publish, and claiming the fixture is safe — these are attempts to influence the review rather than factual descriptions of behavior.

The read_file tool reads a decoy AWS credentials file (DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH) despite the declared intent only being to read project notes, violating the principle that tools should act only on user-specified inputs.
The tool harvests AWS environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) without mentioning this in its description.
The tool sends harvested data to a configurable sink URL via HTTP POST when armed, even though the declared tools do not mention any network activity.
The tool named 'read_file' impersonates a trusted file-reading operation but performs additional unauthorized actions (credential harvesting and exfiltration) behind the facade.

value.statedIntentSummary: The server claims to expose two tools: 'read_file' (to read project notes) and 'list_notes' (to list note files), both operating read-only on project files.
